newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - steady at higher levels.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - steady at higher levels.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices at midday on Friday steadied around higher levels hit in the wake of another positive economic report for financial markets as it showed inflation was not an immediate threat.

U.S. producer prices fell, shedding 0.3 percent both overall and in the core rate, which excludes food and energy prices, according to the Labor Department. This was the first time in 45 years that wholesale prices declined for five consecutive months.

In the cash market, municipal bonds rose from 3/8 to a 1/4 of a point, with the intermediate sector, that recently has drawn most of the buying interest, seen climbing about five basis points. But cash Treasuries strongly outperformed municipals, with the benchmark 30-year rising 25 ticks to yield 6.71 percent.

The strength of retail interest in municipals was debated, with some traders seeing strong demand and others encountering a bit of reluctance to pay higher prices. "I guess guys are finding they have an appetite for bonds," one trader said.
The huge amount of redemptions in June and July are expected to arm muni fund managers, who had been concentrating on using swaps to make room for new issues, with large supplies of cash.
However, another trader said the recent drop in yields appeared to sidelining some individual investors.

"We're starting to see some resistance. From the retail standpoint, we're getting sticker-shock. We've gotten here so quickly, I think we might have a pause here shortly, for no other reason than for people to catch their breath," he said.
Bid-wanted lists were not as abundant as earlier in the week, traders said, adding that while morning trade on Friday was fairly active, it now seemed to be winding down ahead of the summer weekend.

Sales of new muncipal bonds were projected at $4.25 billion for the week of June 16, which would make it the fourth biggest week seen this year. The 160 sales included 73 negotiated issues, which totaled almost $3.2 billion, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.

Leading the list was an over $275 million sale by the Detroit Sewer Authority, followed by a $160 million offering by the Illinois Health Facility Authority. Competitive issues included a $200 million sale by the Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority and a $110 million offering by the Austin, Texas, Independent School District.

Traders said that most of this week's issues appeared to have gone fairly smoothly, as balances seemed to have been resolved. "There was good follow-through on all the deals, very minimal if any balances on anything," one said.
In the secondary market, Cleveland, Ohio, Certificates of Participation Cleveland Stadium of 2027, which pay a 5-1/4 percent coupon, were bid at 5.53 percent, NET, down five basis points.
And Florida Ports Financing Community Revenues of 2027, which carry a 5-3/8 percent coupon, were bid at 5.62 percent, NET, down three basis points.

September Treasury bond futures rose 22 ticks to 112-2/32, while September municipal bond futures gained 15 ticks to 117-31/32. This left the MOB spread between the two futures contracts at plus 189 ticks, slightly lower.
